title: CENTCOM Completes 'Wave of Strikes' on IRGC Targets as Iran Retaliates Against US Bases in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait
detail: US Central Command said it completed a 'wave of strikes' on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets inside Iran — including air-defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities, and communications facilities — beginning Tuesday evening, September 1, 2026 local time, in response to IRGC attempts to mine the Strait of Hormuz and target US forces. Iran retaliated with ballistic missile and drone attacks on US-linked sites in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait; Jordan's air defenses intercepted 13 Iranian ballistic missiles, Kuwait's air defenses responded to drone attacks, and Iran claimed its strike on Jordan's Camp Titin killed a large number of US troops, though US officials said there were no American casualties. President Trump said the US was conducting 'powerful strikes' on Iranian targets and warned further escalation would leave 'very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran.'

media.caption: CENTCOM strikes IRGC targets in Iran as Tehran retaliates against US-linked bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait

title: Bessent Vows to 'Economically Asphyxiate' Iran, Targets IRGC Offshore Assets
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at a G20 finance ministerial discussion moderated by Larry Kudlow, 'We are going to economically asphyxiate this regime,' outlining plans to freeze Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps offshore accounts — including trust-company holdings in the British Virgin Islands — and roughly $100 million in luxury real estate held globally. Bessent said the administration would pursue secondary sanctions barring entities that do business with the IRGC, including airline-leasing companies, from the US dollar system, Federal Reserve wire transfers, and SWIFT access, with any recovered proceeds potentially going to terror victims or the Iranian people. The push came alongside the renewed CENTCOM-IRGC exchange of strikes.

media.caption: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlines plans to freeze IRGC offshore assets and secondary sanctions

title: Trump Meets Oil Refiners at White House to Push Down $4-a-Gallon Gas Prices
detail: President Trump met Tuesday, September 1, 2026, with executives from small, medium, and large oil refiners and distributors at the White House — alongside Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Energy Secretary Chris Wright, and National Energy Dominance Council Executive Director Jarrod Agen — to discuss expanding US refining capacity and lowering pump prices, which have held near $4.10/gallon nationally amid the renewed Iran war. Discussion touched on regulatory rollbacks, faster permitting, and additional refinery investment; Exxon was reportedly not among the invited companies. The meeting followed the administration's Venezuela oil deal, under which the US secured majority control of 65 billion barrels of proven reserves.

media.caption: Trump meets oil refining executives at the White House to discuss lowering gas prices
